risks.risk: Crude oil price volatility and West Asia geopolitical conflict

risks.note: The entire manufacturing business is three-wheeled vehicles for passenger transport, goods carriage and last-mile delivery. There is no diversification into other vehicle categories, so any regulatory, demand or technology shock confined to the three-wheeler segment hits the whole revenue base.

The Company states it does not currently meet the domestic value-addition threshold required to qualify for the PLI scheme for auto and auto components - a scheme that has attracted over Rs 44,000 crore of investment nationally - leaving it structurally disadvantaged against larger OEMs on incentive-supported cost. risks.note: Electric three-wheelers are positioned as the future of the Company, but industry demand in the electric passenger segment is described as incentive-driven and already beginning to moderate, and EV penetration forecasts assume an extended window for government incentives on three-wheelers (PM E-DRIVE extended through FY28). Withdrawal or tapering of incentives is a direct demand risk to the segment the Company is pivoting into. (Read in the Industry Overview routed into the strategy_outlook bundle.)

risks.note: The wholly owned NBFC finances retail buyers of the Company's own three-wheelers and is a material unlisted subsidiary whose net worth exceeds 20% of the Company's net worth. Vehicle sales are therefore partly underwritten by group credit, concentrating both credit risk and cyclical risk in the same customer base of first-time buyers, fleet operators and micro-entrepreneurs. The Company has also given a corporate guarantee for borrowings of a subsidiary.

currentContext.expansion: Atul Auto's expansion in FY 2025-26 was structural rather than greenfield. The Company acquired the L5 Electric Three-Wheeler Vehicle Division of its subsidiary Atul Greentech Private Limited (AGPL) on a slump-sale basis for a consideration of Rs 3,526 Lakhs, effective January 2026 (the Corporate Overview states the acquisition was completed effective January 15, 2026, while the Board's Report states the division was acquired with effect from January 14, 2026). The acquired business manufactures and sells L5 category electric three-wheelers and related components and has a presence in both domestic and international markets; the integration brings the entire electric three-wheeler value chain under a unified operating structure, aligning manufacturing, supply chain, product development and go-to-market, and is expected to shorten the product-to-market cycle, reduce inter-company complexity and streamline business processes. Geographic expansion was the other axis: exports reached 5,517 vehicles across 30+ countries and four continents, with six new market entries during the year - Sri Lanka, Afghanistan, Haiti, Angola, Zimbabwe and Gambia - and channel partnerships reorganised in Mexico, Kenya and South Africa. A strategic partnership with Softlogic Holdings PLC was signed to introduce a new range of passenger and cargo three-wheelers in Sri Lanka, launching with the Atul RIK passenger vehicle, Atul GEM Paxx diesel passenger carrier and Atul GEM Cargo, supported by Softlogic's islandwide sales and after-sales network. For FY27 and beyond the stated plan is to deepen partnerships in existing markets while entering new territories in South-East Asia and East Africa. The distribution footprint comprises a marketing headquarters at Ahmedabad, 8 regional offices, 2 training centres and 500+ domestic sales, service and spare-parts touchpoints, alongside 400+ global touchpoints. Subsidiary Atulease Private Limited, in which the Company holds 80%, is in the preparatory phase and is expected to commence operational-leasing of three-wheelers and other vehicles in the near future. The Company continues to invest in its electric three-wheeler portfolio and in strengthening manufacturing efficiencies. No plant-level capacity addition, commissioning timeline or capex quantum is stated in the routed text; the segment capital-expenditure disclosure that was supplied arrived flagged as ambiguous (no dated period header) and the capital-commitments notes carried no figures, so no rupee capex quantum is usable.

- The L5 Electric Three-Wheeler Undertaking of Atul Greentech Private Limited was acquired mid-year, requiring restatement of prior-year comparatives under Ind AS 103, and the Board's Report states the restated FY 2024-25 figures are not strictly comparable with those originally reported - a reporting discontinuity alongside the operational risk of integrating manufacturing, supply chain, product development and go-to-market functions.
- The wholly owned NBFC finances retail buyers of the Company's own three-wheelers and is a material unlisted subsidiary whose net worth exceeds 20% of the Company's net worth. Vehicle sales are therefore partly underwritten by group credit, concentrating both credit risk and cyclical risk in the same customer base of first-time buyers, fleet operators and micro-entrepreneurs. The Company has also given a corporate guarantee for borrowings of a subsidiary.
- Export volumes grew sharply and now span 30+ countries, but the destination mix is weighted to Africa, Latin America and South/South-East Asia, including markets such as Sudan, DR Congo, Afghanistan, Haiti and Myanmar. Currency, payment, sanctions and political-stability risk in these corridors is structural, and industry commentary notes export growth depends on those economies stabilising.
- Stricter emission norms are due to take effect between 2027 and 2032, pushing the industry towards greener manufacturing and cleaner vehicles; compliance re-engineering across a Diesel/Petrol/CNG/LPG portfolio is a recurring cost and product-obsolescence risk for an ICE-heavy line-up.

themes.title: Auto OEM cycle - CV replacement & PV premiumization
themes.need: GST 2.0 rate rationalization plus an aged CV fleet still frames the replacement cycle, but Q1FY27's real signal is 2W OEMs EXPANDING margin through a commodity shock. TVSMOTOR sold 1.63mn units (+28%) on INR 13,896cr revenue (+38%) while lifting EBITDA margin 30bps to 12.8% having absorbed a ~4% commodity shock with only ~1.5% of price increase (CARE upgraded it AA+ to AAA), and committed 2W capacity from 6.8mn to 8.3mn by Q4FY27. BAJAJ-AUTO set volume/revenue/EBITDA records with margin at 20.9% (+110bps) through ~4.5% commodity inflation AND ~10% of volume lost to a ransomware shutdown, with EV now 30% of domestic revenue at double-digit EBITDA and Chetak EBITDA-positive - a scaled, profitable EV second engine. Commercial mobility is electrifying fastest: TVSMOTOR's 3W EV penetration crossed 40% for the first time. ASHOKLEY's all-time-high CV volumes (220k units, MHCV share 30.8%) carry the CV leg with defence + Switch EV optionality; TMCV/TMPV/SMLMAH/ESCORTS on CV/tractors; APOLLOTYRE/JKTYRE/BALKRISIND/MRF on tyres.
themes.driver: Capacity commissioning against demand (TVSMOTOR 2W to 8.3mn by Q4FY27, BAJAJ-AUTO 7m to 9m+ units); 3W/2W EV penetration inflection; GST-2.0 price-cut demand, aged-fleet replacement and festive 2W/PV.

hero.oneLiner: Atul Auto Limited is one of India's top five three-wheeler manufacturers and the only player in India's three-wheeler segment offering a complete range across all fuel types - Diesel, Petrol, CNG, LPG and Electric.
